title: Access
description: Every way into this gateway, in one place: accounts, OAuth sessions, API keys and registered clients.
loadError: Could not determine your role. Retry.
errorBody: This list failed to load, so it is NOT empty — it is unknown. Retry, or check the server logs.
usersDescription: Every account that exists in this deployment, newest first. The three counts are live access paths: signed-in sessions, unexpired OAuth tokens, and active API keys (including keys that act as this identity).
sessionRefreshedHelp: Last time this account's session cookie was renewed. Better-auth slides that renewal roughly weekly, so it is a coarse signal — an account active minutes ago can read as days old. Use the live-access counts and the API key 'Last used' column for recency.
revokeConfirmDescription: Signs out every session, deletes every OAuth access token and pending authorization code, deactivates every API key that can act as this identity, and forces the Microsoft 365 delegation to re-authenticate. The account itself is KEPT — and it can sign in again immediately. To lock it out, use Disable.
revokeSuccess: Revoked {{sessions}} sessions, {{tokens}} OAuth tokens, {{codes}} authorization codes; deactivated {{keys}} API keys; reset {{m365}} M365 delegations.
disableConfirmDescription: Blocks every gateway path in, starting with this account's next request: sign-in, OAuth authorization, existing OAuth and bearer tokens, API keys — including admin keys acting as this account — the admin console, and the MCP proxy. Nothing is deleted and nothing is invalidated: the account, its history, its owned resources and its credentials are all preserved for the audit record, Enable restores access at any time, and Revoke is what tears down the sessions, tokens and keys permanently.
enableConfirmDescription: Restores the ability to sign in. Any sessions, tokens and API keys revoked earlier stay revoked — this only removes the lock.
deleteConfirmLead: This is irreversible, and the deletion is NOT limited to this account. Everything below is destroyed by the database cascade:
deleteCrossUserWarning: Other users' endpoints and API keys die with this account: an endpoint owned by someone else living in one of this account's namespaces, and any API key that acts as this identity or is scoped to a doomed endpoint. Deleting a CI or sync identity will revoke another administrator's production key.
deleteCrossUserNone: No other user's resources are affected by this deletion.
deleteConsiderDisable: If this is an active investigation, Disable preserves the account and its evidence while still locking the attacker out.
deleteImpactFailed: Could not calculate the blast radius. Do not proceed until you know what this deletes.
tokensDescription: Unexpired access tokens — who is connected through an OAuth client right now. Token values are never shown; revoke by deleting the client, or by revoking or disabling the user.
apiKeysDescription: Every API key across all users. Only a non-reversible prefix is shown. Mint, rename and revoke keys on the API Keys page.
clientsDescription: Clients that may complete an authorization flow against this gateway. Register and delete clients on the OAuth Clients page.

groups.title: Access Groups
groups.description: Named groups that decide which OAuth users may reach which endpoints. API keys are unaffected.
groups.heading: Groups
groups.createGroupDescription: A group is a reusable set of people. Map endpoints to it, then switch those endpoints on.
groups.createFailed: Could not create the access group
groups.nameHelp: Free text, unique across the gateway. Names appear in the audit log.
groups.noGroupsDescription: Until a group exists and an endpoint is switched on, every OAuth user reaches every endpoint they already could.
groups.deleteFailed: Could not delete the access group
groups.deleteConfirmDescription: Deletes "{{name}}" and every grant it carries. Anyone who reached a restricted endpoint only through this group loses access immediately.
groups.membersHelp: People in this group reach every endpoint mapped to it. Administrators reach every endpoint regardless.
groups.endpointsHelp: Mapping an endpoint here grants it to this group's members. It only takes effect once that endpoint is switched on.
groups.endpointFailed: Could not update the endpoint mapping
groups.scopeNote: A group grants or denies a whole endpoint. To give an audience a narrower tool set, curate a second namespace and publish a second endpoint over it, then map the group to that one.
groups.restrictedDescription: When on, an OAuth user reaches this endpoint only if they are an administrator or belong to a group mapped to it. Saved on its own, not with the rest of this dialog. It applies to the next request; an already-open notification stream keeps running until it disconnects, though no tool call can land through it.
groups.noOauthWarning: This endpoint does not accept OAuth callers, so this switch has no effect today. Access groups gate OAuth users only; turn OAuth on for this endpoint if you want the switch to do anything.
groups.apiKeysStillPass: This endpoint also accepts API keys, and those are not affected by access groups. The switch narrows OAuth callers only; every API-key holder still reaches this endpoint.
groups.noGroupsWarning: This endpoint is restricted but no group is mapped to it, so only administrators can reach it.
groups.mappedGroupsLabel: Groups that may reach this endpoint
groups.apiKeyNote: API keys are not affected by this. A key is minted by an administrator and already carries its own per-endpoint scoping.
